utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have appearances starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, General. Good morning, everybody in and around the courtroom. Barney Thomas, Carmela Javier, and Dan Saxon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to all. On behalf of Mr. Perisic, Novak Lukic, Gregor Guy-Smith, Tina Drolec and Boris Zorko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Good morning, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Once again, and I know you know it, but I just want to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration that you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do know that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, you were on an objection yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think as far as my objection is concerned, Mr. Thomas might probably be in a position to provide a better reply than myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, I have's discussed the matter my learned friend after with closed yesterday. I withdraw the question that was on the table as at the moment the objection was made. I will return to the document but do so in a different fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, good morning. We will continue with our questions again regarding your testimony. Can I please just repeat what I suggested to you at the start of our questions yesterday, which is please listen very closely to the question that I'm asking you, please answer only that question otherwise I will need to interrupt you and we will need to start again. Also if you need a break at any stage, of course, please just let us know. If there are any questions or if there's anything about my questioning that you do not understand, please say so, and I will put it a different way for you. Once again, are we clear?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is very clear. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we please have document D246 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, General, you looked at this document on Friday from memory, and you described it as a schedule that depicted -- well, as the title says, The numerical strength in May 1995 of the 30th Personnel Centre. And you pointed to a total, I think, of 2.276 officers who you described as officers receiving their salaries through the 30th Personnel Centre. And you made a comment at that point which was however to that number you also need to add the contract soldiers. And what I want to ask you, sir, is how are the figures affected by the addition of contract soldiers associated with the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm looking at this table, and it was my administration that produced it. I was its head, and I believe this happened back in 1995. The only time I stepped in was about this figure 2.276 and then 146 was added to that, totalling 2.421. The discrepancy here, you talked about contract soldiers. The contract soldiers are part of this group of persons whose salaries are paid through the 30th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And just briefly, General, for Their Honours, can you explain the difference between a contract soldier and an officer?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The professional officer in NCO is taken on with no fixed term, once they are out of secondary school and military academy. The contract soldier, on the other hand, is a soldier who served his regular military term, and then in keeping with the regulations at some later date, is he admitted or taken on by the army on a professional basis, but only for a fixed term depending on what the regulations stipulate, three, five more years.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We see at least in May 1995 there's only a small number of contract soldiers. Do you know whether contract soldiers were sent regularly through the 30th Personnel Centre to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps on an individual basis, but I wouldn't call that regular. I'm not exactly sure what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you the question another way. At any given time did the number of officers assigned through the 30th Personnel Centre greatly exceed the number of contract soldiers; is that a fair comment?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. May I provide an explanation, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, let me ask you the question another way. The 30th Personnel Centre --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The figure was always within that range, 150, 160, depending on the point in time we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, that's what I was trying to ask. Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we go again, please, Mr. Registrar, to P851.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, General, you will recognise this document when it comes on the screen as one we were looking at last evening. First, can you confirm for us that it is signed by General Perisic?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer this one, you say I saw this one yesterday, whereas I don't think I did. I don't think I've ever seen this one before.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. General, you may be correct, this may be the document that we were just about to place on the screen when we adjourned last night.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the question is concerned, whether General Perisic signed this, you can look at his signature and that confirms it, yes. But may I just be given a chance to read through it?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You'll see that the document records the transfer of 500.000 dinar from the General Staff through the General Staff's accounting centre to the VRS Main Staff for salaries of 30th Personnel Centre officers during the period of the sanctions imposed by the FRY on the RS. Do you see that? Or do you agree?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not quite sure that Mr. Thomas's question reflects the substance of the document. Perhaps if he tries to take a slightly more specific approach in interpreting what the document says. Or perhaps his theory is different from what the document actually says, in which case he should clearly state that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect to my learned friend, I was asking the general for his response to that proposition, not my learned friend. I have a document, I've suggested to him what I say the document says. It's for the general to accept or reject that proposition. If the general doesn't think this is what the letter records, that's exactly what I've asked him, sir, do you agree that this is what the letter tells us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, do you agree with my interpretation of this document?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Esteemed Mr. Prosecutor, it's not about interpretation here, it's about the wording. As for the wording of the document, I'm reading it. As far as that is concerned, yes. As far as an explanation is concerned, I'll try to take the following approach in answering: May I answer the question in two parts?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, while I was being examined by Mr. Lukic he was adamant that you I should explain the general purposes and tasks of certain organisational units of the defence ministry. Under the rules on their respective areas of competence, I briefly explained that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, I'm sorry, please pause. I understand what you feel you need to do, but we need to stick to the question. Let me rephrase this so we can take this slowly. Let's look at the first line. In mid-September 1994, this is the period during the period under which the Republika Srpska was under sanctions imposed by the FRY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The Supreme Defence Council made a decision to suspend payment of salaries to your people, and in the context of this letter, given that it's General Perisic writing to General Mladic or writing to the -- yes, writing to General Mladic, would you agree that refers to salaries to members of the 30th Personnel Centre fighting in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The next line says that there has been an agreement between General Mladic and General Perisic to send 500.000 dinar, which was done on the 21st of September. The money was collected by General Tomic, and it's recorded in the General Staff, VJ General Staff accounting centre as a temporary payment. I'm reading from the document, so no doubt you don't have any dispute with what I've just read, correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you just read out is exactly what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we go to document P2770, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I be allowed to ask a question. I don't think I actually finished my sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If you didn't finish your answer, sir, please finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You stopped my in midstream. I was trying to --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, pause, please. I'm not trying to prevent you from saying anything, but I need you to stick to the questions that I asked and that's why I had to stop you midstream, all right. I was looking for you to focus on a particular subject and that is why I point stopped and I re-asked the questioned again. All right. We need to get through your testimony, sir. I don't want you here all week. None of us want you here all week. All right. Please, you will have the opportunity under re-examination to answer any questions that Mr. Lukic feels should be put to you. While I'm asking you questions, sir, just answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we please have document P2770. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, I'm told that's partly a confidential document. We need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If we could do that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, have you had the opportunity to read this document? I see the original is difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. I wonder, Mr. Registrar, it is a difficult copy to read on the screen as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you need it any larger, General?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read this, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We'll take that off the screen. I won't ask you questions about it, General. Last week when you were talking about the 30th Personnel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you still want to stay in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, we can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Thomas, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, do I understand your position on the 30th Personnel Centre members to be that once they are appointed to the 30th Personnel Centre and once they are then within the VRS chain of command that all of the regulation of their status or issues was performed by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was certainly the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. I want to look, please, at Exhibit P2417, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, what we see on the screen is a decision of the VRS Main Staff disciplinary military court or the disciplinary military court attached to the air force and PVO command of the VRS, involving a number of individuals, but one of those you will see in the middle of the first paragraph is a Captain Antic. You see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we go, please, to -- stay on that page in the B/C/S, Your Honours, but if -- thank you, go to page 2, we have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You will see that in the first paragraph under "Are Guilty" you will find they were found guilty of abandoning their unit. You see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if we go to the number 2 at the very bottom of the page that you are looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, we'll need to go to the next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You will see that the sentence imposed for accused number 2, which is Mr. Antic, is the loss of service status as an active serviceman. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The next document I want to go to, please, is P2418.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, on the basis of that decision, in other words, the decision finding Mr. Antic guilty of desertion, there is a recommendation to end professional military service. And this is what we are looking at on the screen. Can you tell me the purpose of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a serious disciplinary infraction. The person who left his unit and his duty without proper authorisation, the military disciplinary court imposed a disciplinary measure by removing this person from active service, the person you named a minute ago. In cases such as that, the appropriate officer from the personnel centre must start termination proceedings, and that is precisely what the document shows.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we go, please, to document 2419, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, based on the recommendation issued by the 30th Personnel Centre, itself based on the VRS Main Staff disciplinary court decision, we have this order issued by the chief of the personnel administration, the General Staff of the VJ, terminating the service of Zoran Antic, and the reason for the end of service is recorded in the middle of the page we are looking at, "absent without leave for five consecutive days." So is this the net result of his being found guilty in the VRS disciplinary court?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a correction I'll have to make though. He did not just leave his position, he left the entire unit, not having been authorised to do that. Under Article 7, paragraph 1 of the Law on the Armed Forces, this constitutes a reason for termination of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And because he was a member of the VJ transferred to the 30th Personnel Centre, if the VRS wanted him terminated, that had to happen in the VJ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the VJ, but please allow me to complete my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes. Please do.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday we discussed this. With a decision of this kind on the termination of the professional military service, he ceased to enjoy any of the status-related issues, and this is why this particular body had to issue such a decision. So this only related to the status-related issues or entitlements.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Effectively you are saying that the VJ had to do what the VRS said in this particular circumstance, namely terminate him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It confirmed the decision of the military disciplinary court.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we have document P2765 on the screen, please. Sorry, Your Honours, wrong document. P2420.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We have another VRS military disciplinary court decision, this time of the court attached to the air force and PVO. You will see from the document in front of you that a number of personnel including Major Vujic are again found guilty of absconding from their unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, we will need to go to page 2 in the English to see the finding that they have been found guilty of absconding from their unit, and that is found on the final paragraph of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Once again, General, we have a familiar sentence, if you look at number 3 -- sorry, number 2, at the bottom of your page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if we could please go to the next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We will see that under number 2, Major Vujic, in fact all of them, but the person I'm interested for the moment is Major Vujic, is sentenced to the disciplinary punishment of loss of service status as an active serviceman. You see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So if what you said about the previous person we were look at, Captain Antic is correct, Major Vujic would have had his service terminated both in the VRS and in the VJ as a result of this decision; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a judgement. The judgement must be respected and this is true of both of them, but you have to read the entire statement of reasons of this judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we go, please, to P2421, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, General, as you see this letter, you will see that it comes from --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please enlarge this a little bit. It is rather difficult to read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the witness to know and possibly Mr. Thomas also wanted to explain this, who issued this document, because the way in which this is placed on the screen now in B/C/S it is unclear who signed this document or where it came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Is that the top of the document, Mr. Registrar, in B/C/S? All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, take a moment to read the document and then we will put the English version on the screen as well.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, could we see the text further down. Thank you. I have read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could perhaps the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I haven't seen the second page. I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Can we please -- thank you. Can you confirm for us what we are looking at is a letter from VJ air force and PVO command to the personnel administration of the General Staff of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the text says.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And what they are talking about is the decision that we have just been looking at, the judgement entered by the military disciplinary court against Vujic and others, with a sentence as termination of service, correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we go to page 2 in the English, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that this should result in their termination in the VJ, but we don't need to -- we don't need to take you through each paragraph in this letter, but the balance -- does the balance of the letter comprise a request from the commander to retain these men in the VJ because they are still valuable to the VJ? In other words, to ignore the VRS disciplinary court decision?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This documents of the commander of the air force and PVO is in my belief just a letter sent to the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army. When we are talking about military disciplinary courts, we need to know that they are independent, and in my mind he was supposed to address a higher military disciplinary court, rather than the General Staff of the VJ. So in this letter, he is simply asking for the court decisions to be revised. This was addressed to the personnel administration which is not competent to decide on such matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, the commander of the -- or the commander of the air force who read the decision makes the comment, does he not, and we can see it, Your Honours, the first full paragraph in the English that is on the screen at the moment. He makes -- and I appreciate this is his own observation, the observation: "That the proceedings of the trial and the rendering of the judgements were not conducted in accordance with the regulations on military discipline in the VJ. Namely, the persons involved are members of the RV and PVO who had been sent temporarily to work in the units of the 30th Personnel Centre. And, therefore, in our opinion, the conducting of proceedings for the violation of military discipline by the above members of the RV and PVO is in the jurisdiction of the military disciplinary court attached to the command of the air force." That is part of this argument, is it not? Yes or no, sir?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is his argument, but once again, I would like to point out that the commander of the air force --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Pause, sir.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand this is only a letter from him to the Main Staff. That is why I'm limiting my questions to the matters that I have limited them to. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like to read this letter to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. So this letter is dated the 29th of January, 1996. The officers concerned including Lieutenant-Colonel Vujic have been found guilty and sentenced to termination.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So what I want to go now to, please, is P2422.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Which is coming. Now, General, what we see here is the order terminating service for Mr. Vujic, but it is not dated 1996. He remained in service until 12 October 2005, and was terminated on the basis that he had reached 30 years of pensionable service. So my question to you is, does not that show that he remained in service in the VJ notwithstanding the documents that we have just been reviewing?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask this order to be enlarged because I have difficulties reading this statement of reasons. Thank you. Could we scroll this down, please. Could I now answer to your question, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: My question, sir, is notwithstanding the documents that we have just been reviewing, clearly Mr. Vujic remained in the service of the VJ until this order was issued, whereupon he was terminated because he had reached 30 pensionable years of service?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this document says until that it should be submitted to him until the 31st of October, 2005. However -- but this is my speculation. Probably during the procedure of the termination of his service he got ill. In the statement of reasons in paragraph 2, if you can see this, please allow me to read this out. Yes, this is the portion I'm talking about. Here it says that the above-mentioned person was pursuant to the finding of the medical commission of the 29th of September, was found to be permanently incapacitated to carry out his service. And in line with the decision of the minister of defence and then have the reference number of 28th of May, 2005, item 1, subparagraph (2), his professional military service shall be terminated to professional military serviceman who have been partially incapacitated and who have reached 30 serviceable years, well, for benefit, regardless of their rank or age. Given that I do not have any other documents here before me from which I could conclude what it is that actually happened, I can only conclude that during the procedure of his termination, this particular person got ill, that he was, therefore, treated and that he was finally found to be incapacitated for his military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. General, let me ask you the question a slightly different way. Go, please, to the first paragraph under the statement of reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And that's on the previous page, Mr. Registrar, in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We know from that first paragraph it was established that he was in service without break since 22 July 1977 and has earned over 30 serviceable years for welfare benefit.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And your question is?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, that's what we know from the document, correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what the document states, but this is linked to Article 107, paragraph 1, item 1 of the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia, so the person that is found by the relevant military medical review board as unfit will be permanently terminated and such a finding is obligatory for his superior to adopt appropriate decision terminating his service.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please go quickly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please have Exhibit P2765 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, you can see that this is a document sent from the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska to the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we could go to the last -- sorry, the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Page 4 in the English, and the signature page in the B/C/S. I'm not sure what page that is, Mr. Registrar. It's probably page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature of General Mladic at the bottom of that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recognise his signature. I'm not aware of what his signature looked like, but I see that this document was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we could go back to page 1 in each version, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And once again, if we could enlarge this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We can do this paragraph by paragraph, Mr. Registrar, if we start with paragraph 1, please, the first paragraph of the document. And if we can have the English on the screen as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't read this. It is just too small. If we could enlarge this. Or if you have this document in a hard copy version possibly I could read it then. This way I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do. I have a single copy. It's marked, I need to show it to my learned friends first. I understand that this can be done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, I can tell you that we don't need to read the entire letter. I can -- the answer to my question -- to answer the question that follows, you really only need to read the first paragraph and then the paragraph -- or the first half of the paragraph numbered 1 that follows. My question, General, is this: Does General Mladic's complaint to the General Staff not suggest that the VRS were not as free to regulate the status of -- or to regulate the status and issues relating to 30th Personnel Centre members as you have said?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: What is he complaining about?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I could read in this brief time, he complains that the requested men are not being regularly sent from the command chain of the Army of Yugoslavia into the command chain of the Army of Republika Srpska. And he is also saying that he shouldn't be continuously asked to send requests for this to the Supreme Defence Council or Chief of the General Staff. So he is simply asking for the administrative burden to be decreased since he is saying all the regulations have been harmonised with the relevant criteria, and he says that all the documents concerning their status-related issues have already been submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: He complains also, does he not, about the need to have personnel transferred with the approval of the competent officer in the General Staff of the VJ? He complains about the problems that having to go through that step causes, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but he says that these transfers are made through the 30th Personnel Centre in line with the regulations and orders stipulating the way in which these personnel centres operate.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, if we could have that document off the screen, and we can go back into public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, sometime last week you discussed the agreement on special parallel relations.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar, could we please retrieve the document, or madam usher, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You discussed the agreement on special parallel relations between the FRY and the RS, part of which covered the assumption of full responsibility, if I can call it that, of soldiers previously administered by the 30th Personnel Centre. These were now to be, or those records and the payment of them were to be taken over by the VRS as a result of the annex to the special parallel relations agreement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Have I stated the position correctly, sir? General, you may answer this.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is slightly confusing. It's complicated. I don't think I even understood fully. Can you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was precisely the reason I sprang to my feet, I think it was about the interpretation. The interpreter got it right, but there were some ambiguities left. It is a complex question, after all. I think it might be a good idea if Mr. Thomas could just break it down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You spoke of the negotiations and discussions that took place in 2001 regarding the drafting and implementation of the agreement on special parallel relations between the FRY and the RS. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Part of the special parallel relations agreement contained an annex which governed how the VRS was to take over the records and payment of salaries of service of officers previously administered through the 30th Personnel Centre, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not what the agreement says.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, was there not an agreement between the FRY and the RS over the VRS receiving aid from the FRY, financial aid from the FRY for the purpose of paying VRS salaries?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that calls for a different answer, an altogether different answer. Certain financial aid will be exchanged between the countries, but it won't be the VJ paying it, rather the VRS alone. That is the substance of the agreement. This is an agreement between the two governments. Up to a certain point in time aid will be provided. When that aid will stop is a different issue altogether, but it's not the VJ making any payments, especially not along the same principle that had been applied up to that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we just make sure that we've got the record correct. Page 22, line 5, did you say but it won't be the VJ paying it rather the VRS alone, or did you say something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can't remember what exactly that paragraph of the agreement says. If I had it in front of me, I could quote it for you. What I do remember, however, and what I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a minute. I'm not asking you whether you remember the paragraph. I'm asking you what you just said. You said here, I'm trying to make sure that you have been correctly interpreted, sir. You have been interpreted as, or transcribed rather --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it was not the correct interpretation. May I repeat, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, please, just that sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The VJ would stop making any payments to members of the VRS and the Serbian Krajina, but here specifically the VRS, who had been paid through the 30th Personnel Centre up until that point in time. Nevertheless, a financial aid package was agreed between the two governments or the relevant ministries for certain aid to be awarded, administered, and certain financial amounts. However, the salaries would only be paid and calculated by the VRS and no one else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you talk of financial aid. I don't know what form this financial aid takes. I'm asking you, can you just listen to my question. You have said in answer to a question by

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: "Well, that calls for a different answer, an altogether different answer. Certain financial aid will be exchanged between the countries, but it won't be the VJ paying it, rather the VRS alone." Now, I want to find out whether that's what you said, or did you say something slightly different? Did you say the VRS alone --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Perhaps just to clarify that, General. As a result of this agreement, the VRS and the VRS alone were responsible for paying the salaries of all VRS officers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I'll answer why. You didn't ask me about the specific time-period. You said all members of the army. From what point in time on?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, pause, think about my question. I'm not talking about time-periods. As a result of this agreement that we have just been discussing, that you have spent the last ten minutes discussing, as a result of this agreement, it was the VRS now who were to be responsible for paying the salaries of officers within the VRS, including those previously administered by the 30th Personnel Centre; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: To assist them in doing so, the FRY government would provide financial aid to the RS government; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Is it true that the continued provision of this aid, no longer in the form of salaries but in the form of aid from one government to another, still caused the international community some concern, and I'm talking particularly about the United States?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never heard that sort of information. Nothing indicating that. At least not about the results of this agreement. There was a meeting, though, that occurred later on following the conclusion of the agreement. It wasn't about interventions on anyone's part. Rather, we were provided additional information. It's about Warren Montgomery who asked for a meeting with the federal Defence ministry of the FRY to see what sort of aid was at stake here. The meeting was held at the Federation palace, what used to be call the Federation palace back then. I saw the document and I know what Montgomery's position was. He was particularly at pains to point out as follows: Croatia's army --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Pause, General. Pause, General. General, we recall your testimony on this document, and in that meeting Ambassador Montgomery referred to concern, at least back in the United States, among influential quarters that aid was continued to be paid from the FRY to the RS, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never learned of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, let's have a look, please, at document -- let me check, Your Honours. I'm sorry. 251. D251. And the paragraph I want to look at, please, is on page 2 of both documents, I think. Sorry, Mr. Registrar, we have two B/C/S versions on our screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you see the paragraph, General, which refers to the ambassador being informed by a senior official that assistance in all forms of funding of the VRS will end this year? First of all, just tell me if you've found that paragraph in the document.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please specify which paragraph to avoid going through the entire text. Do you mean the last one?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: This is a document you are familiar with. We went through it yesterday. What I will do is I will read you the paragraph that I'm interested in. All right. This is how it reads: The ambassador has allegedly been informed by a senior official -- sorry, has allegedly been informed by a -- I'll try it again, I'm sorry, Your Honours. "The ambassador has allegedly been informed by 'a senior official' in our government that assistance and all forms of funding of the VRS will end this year. This has been conveyed to relevant US authorities. The secretary of state has informed congress. However, it follows from the agreement with the Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence that the funding will continue next year, so 'the highest state organs of the US have been misinformed.' In the US there are skeptics (but not in the government) who are doubtful about changes in the FRY; they are influential and are mainly present and non-governmental organisations and in congress." Now, let's not mince words about this, General. There was concern that money was still going to the VRS, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... take a break. We'll come back at quarter to. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, I want to move on to a different topic now. In the course of your testimony you referred to this concept of unity of command, and I just want to make sure that I understand the concept of unity of command as distinct, for example, from the chain of command. Am I right in saying that when you talk about unity of command, you are talking about the fact that a soldier has a single superior from whom he is taking orders?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you please answer again, sir, into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I have to answer the other question too.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just pause, General, we'll get to that. And the principle of unity of command is so that any given officer knows exactly who he is supposed to receive orders from; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Depending on where that soldier or officer is in the chain of command, however, there may be more officers in the chain of command above that soldier's commanding officer, can't there?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but allow me to explain why.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each officer appointed to certain duty has a superior officer above him, only one. But there is also another who is the superior of his direct superior. This ultimately superior officer may issue an order to the first officer. Nevertheless, the first officer is under an obligation to immediately report this to his direct superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could you explain that for Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. In a military hierarchy, there are certain relations between servicemen. This depends on the persons or the soldier's duty. We are talking about subordinates and superiors. A superior officer is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, just wait. What I do want to understand is you have an officer or a soldier with a direct superior above him, and this superior has his own superior, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, what I don't understand is what you mean by "this ultimately superior" I guess you wanted to say this ultimate superior officer may issue an order to the first officer, nevertheless the first officer is under an obligation to immediately report to his direct superior. Now, the direct superior to whom he must report is the same one who has just given the instruction. If you say to me a superior who wants to give instructions to a person who is not his direct subordinate, would give instructions to his immediate subordinate who in turn would pass the instructions to the next subordinate; is that what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but if I may, just a brief explanation to put this in the most graphic terms possible. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic is on his feet so he takes precedent over you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we have a certain amount of confusion because of inaccurate interpreting, and also I was listening to the interpretation of your question in the Serbian, Your Honour, and also the witness's previous answer. I think the problem is "ultimately superior" and the witness was using the term the "second superior."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in order to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... do you have a suggestion as to -- can you tell us what was intended to be the message?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe if the witness used an example to illustrate this, that would be convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just by way of an example, I am a brigade commander. The corps commander is my direct superior. My second superior is the army commander, and my third superior is the chief, the General Staff of the VJ. So I talked about the second superior, in this case the army commander. And the situation is this, he gives me an order to carry out a certain assignment. I will carry out the assignment, nevertheless, I'm under an obligation to report this to my direct superior, who in this case is the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if we stay with the same example, General, let's say the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ wished to order you as brigade commander to do something, he would issue an order to the army commander, who would pass on the order to the corps commander, who would pass on the order to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, that would be the regular procedure. But there is also a different parallel procedure applied in exceptional situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now can you tell us about that, sir.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the needs of service allow or require a special interest and one cannot afford to wait, at that point in time in that unit one tracks down the Chief of the General Staff, and I have a brigade in mind, and he cannot wait for the corps commander to come and issue an order, that has to do with the organisation of life and work in that brigade, rather, he will be issuing a direct order, and I will be carrying it out. Nevertheless, I'm under an obligation once I've carried out the order to inform my direct superior, that being the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. General, you spoke last week about your particular situation, namely that you were a VJ officer, but you were assigned to work for a period of time in the MOD. You told us that you were assigned within the MOD to various positions by order of the minister of defence or his appropriate delegate. Do I understand your testimony correctly?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. You told us that after your time -- first of all, let me just so that we are clear, while you were serving in the MOD you retained your status as a VJ officer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was assigned as an officer to the MOD, and my status in the service was regulated by the Ministry of Defence. At that moment I entered the chain of command of the Ministry of Defence and I was out from the chain of command of the General Staff of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm not talking about chain of command for the moment, General. Did you remain a VJ officer while you were in the MOD? Was your status that of a VJ officer?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So, for example, when you retired your years of pensionable service in the VJ included not just your time spent within the VJ, but also your time spent in the MOD; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. The order transferring you from the MOD to the VJ was issued by General Perisic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was transferred in 1984 on the order of the chief of personnel administration of the SSNO who was in charge of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just pause, General. I think we have a miscommunication. After your time in the MOD, you were transferred, I think in 1995, to the General Staff of the VJ; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but you first of all said from the General Staff to the ministry, and I said upon whose order that was. And this is the second issue when I was transferred from the ministry to the General Staff. So which of these two situations would you like me to describe?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, we had a translation error. The question I want you to -- the situation I want you to look at is that when you were transferred from the MOD to the General Staff of the VJ in 1995. This is the situation we are talking about. The operative document effecting that transfer was an order issued by General Perisic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I can provide an answer in order to explain this. The Chief of General Staff of the VJ, General Perisic, requested an approval of the minister of defence for me to be assigned to the General Staff of the VJ. The minister issued a written approval for me to be transferred from the ministry to the General Staff. Pursuant to that approval, the chief of general took me over, entered me into his chain of command, and thus I became an officer of the VJ in the General Staff of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, what you have not told us in that answer is by what formal document was this transfer effected?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a document issued by the minister of defence stating his approval for my assignment at the General Staff. So it was the document issued by the minister followed by the document issued by the Chief of General Staff with which he regulated my position in the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. So if we looked at your personnel file, in the time that you were working at the MOD, your personnel file would show that assignments to various positions were made by order of the minister; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Are you saying that if we looked at your personnel file, your assignment from the MOD to the General Staff of the VJ would be attributed in your personnel file to an order of the minister of defence, or would it be attributed to the order of General Perisic?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, without an order of the minister of defence, the Chief of the General Staff could not have done it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, I understand that. Listen to my question. I understand that approval of the minister was required. Was the document formalising the transfer the order issued by General Perisic? Is that the formal order required for recognition of your transfer to the General Staff from the MOD? Yes or no, sir?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is the interpretation that is causing this misunderstanding, but as I said, without the document issued by the minister, General Perisic could not assign me to the General Staff. I'm not sure if I'm making myself clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me ask a question here. Sir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You gave an answer, and I would like you to look at the transcript on the -- if you can read it, page 32 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't read English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right. Page 32, line 4, you said: "This was a document issued by the minister of defence stating his approval for my assignment at the General Staff. So it was the document issued by the minister followed by the document issued by the Chief of the General Staff with which he regulated my position in the service." My question to you is: What is the nature of this document by the Chief of the General Staff that followed the minister's document, the minister's approval?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document of the Chief of the General Staff, Your Honour, has the form of an order; whereas, the document issued by the minister of defence could be an order or a decision, so these were the documents regulating assignments and statuses in the service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what did the Chief of the General Staff order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chief of the General Staff wrote an order, or rather, that order was prepared by the personnel administration in order to determine my establishment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, we want to finish. We know somebody prepares it, it's the order of the Chief of General Staff. What did it say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was the order on assignment at the duty of the chief of administration for housing issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, this order is supposed to be dealing with your transfer from the minister of defence to the VJ. What did it order you to do, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As soon as I received the order on assignment from the Chief of the General Staff, I had to report to the duty at the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is the document that triggered your move from the Ministry of Defence to the VJ General Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it wasn't triggered because my situation in the service was already regulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It was the last document that you had to get before you left the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I wonder, please, if we could have P197 on the screen. And particularly, Your Honours, I'm looking at -- if I could just have a moment, sir. Page 38 in the English and page 13 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, General, you will be familiar with this document. It is the Law on the VJ.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I can't read this, the font is too small.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. General, I will read you the relevant provision. I'm looking at Article 152, and subparagraph (5). So it reads as follows: "The Chief of General Staff and the commanding officers of units or institutions designated by him shall: Decide on the assignment of professional members of the army to duties outside the army, while assignment to the Federal Ministry of Defence shall be carried out at the request or with the approval of the federal minister of defence or a commanding officer authorised by him." You are familiar with this article?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And does this cover the situation that you have been -- that you found yourself in? In other words, that the transfers to and from the VJ General Staff to the MOD were governed by this article?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is a reverse case. In this case people were moved from the General Staff to the MOD, and it discusses the authorities of the Chief of General Staff and the commanding officers authorised by him. Previously we discussed the contrary situation. For example, if you allow me --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just pause, General. No, I understand. So there are two situations contemplated here where there is assignment to the MOD, that is with the approval of the minister of defence, and any other assignment outside the army does not require obviously the approval of the federal minister of defence, it is just done by the Chief of the General Staff or his delegates. Am I right in my interpretation?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an exception made if somebody had to be assigned to the Federal Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I want to move, please, to another article. Article 181 which is on page 45 of the English and page 16 of the B/C/S, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I want to discuss, General, the situation as it relates to discipline or the disciplining of individuals assigned outside the army. You as someone who was assigned to the MOD was assigned outside the army in accordance with Article 152 as we have just seen. And your testimony yesterday -- my apologies, last week, was that those assigned to the 30th Personnel Centre and the 40th Personnel Centre were to be likened to those transferred outside the army. I want to begin, please, with Article 181. If you had committed a disciplinary offence while you were serving in the MOD, you told us last week that it would be the federal minister of defence who was responsible for disciplining you. Do you I understand your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And that is on the basis of Article 181?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: In respect of all other situations, it's the army commander or a senior officer holding an equal or higher position under paragraph 2. Am I reading the section correctly?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I want to move, General, please to Article 177.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Which is page 15 in the B/C/S, the same page in ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And as that's coming, General, we don't need to look at them, but the Law on the VJ sets out a number of things which would constitute a disciplinary offence, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but in the Law on the Army, there is a particular provision dealing with offences. Previously you spoke about disciplinary responsibility though.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. I will rephrase my question. In the Law of the VJ there are provisions which set out what constitutes disciplinary offences?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. We have Article 177 I think on the screen for you now. So if you could cast your eye over that. This confirms that we have within the VJ military disciplinary courts who are authorised to try individuals for disciplinary offences. And under Article 178, we see where these military disciplinary courts are. We have courts of first instance established at the General Staff and at the commands of the army, air force, and anti-defence and at the navy, and there is a higher military disciplinary court at the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I want to move, please, to Article 53 which is on page 5 of the B/C/S, Your Honours, and on page 13 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Before I ask you any questions about Article 53, General, was General Perisic required to discipline members or soldiers, officers assigned to the 30th Personnel Centre if they had committed any disciplinary offences while serving in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. I just want to explore that with you for a moment. Under Article 53, the second paragraph reads: "A professional officer or non-commissioned officer assigned outside the army shall have the same rights and duties of professional officers and non-commissioned officers assigned to the army, unless otherwise stipulated by this law." Now, you are familiar with this provision. I think in your testimony you referred to the need to have soldiers assigned to the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres acting in a professional way. So Article 53 doesn't merely confer them the same rights, it also imposes upon them the same duties. Am I correct in my interpretation?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second paragraph, as you interpreted it, is not correct. May I provide an explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No, I will ask you the question in another way, General. Does a professional officer or non-commissioned officer assigned outside the army have the same rights as a professional officer assigned to the army? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Does he also have the same duty? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which duties are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, let's get to that. My question is, looking at Article 53, sir, does he have the same duties as an officer in the army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this second paragraph of Article 53 when it says that they shall have the same rights and duties, the rights refers to the entitlements issuing from the service in the army, and duties refers to duties of professional officers, which they have as professionals. So in relation to other citizens, they have different duties regarding their behaviour, military discipline, their attitude towards people and everything else, so they have to protect the honour of a military officer. So it is not the duty of, say, commanding over a certain unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand that, General. The point is, those assigned outside the army have the same duties as those in the army under Article 53, don't they?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just said what this duties refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just pause, General. Just pause. Article 53, second paragraph contains one sentence. This is what I'm talking about. I'm not talking about anything else except what this one article says, this one sentence says. You follow me?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do follow you. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the sentence says that officers assigned outside the army shall have the same duties as officers assigned to the army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the duties that I listed before.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, it says the same duties as officers in the army. You must accept this, do you not?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move, please, to Article 159, which is on page 39, Your Honours, of the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. So we know from the provisions that there are disciplinary courts, that with the exception of the MOD the army commander or senior officer holding the same or equal or higher position is responsible for discipline in the army. I want to go now to Article 159, which reads: "A service member who violates military discipline, a service member who violates military discipline in the performance of his service or in connection with the performance of his service shall be held responsible for disciplinary infractions or disciplinary offences." Now, General, before I ask you any questions about this, let me check that we agree on the interpretation of this provision. Does this provision mean that any service member, in other words anyone in service in the VJ who violates military discipline, shall be held responsible; am I right in my interpretation?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we are talking about military service members who violate military discipline in the performance of their service or in connection with the performance of their service. They shall be held responsible for disciplinary infractions or disciplinary offences, so we are talking about members of the military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So was the answer to my question yes, you agree with my interpretation?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the explanation that I provided, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, I want to look finally then, please, at what constitutes service in the VJ, or members in service.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And for that, please, we will go to Article 8, which is page 2 of the B/C/S and page 3, Your Honours, of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, the first line, let's look at Article 8, the first line is straightforward enough. What I'm interested in is the second sentence of Article 8: "Service in the army shall also include military and other duties in the Federal Ministry of Defence." Now, this was your situation, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It shall also include military and other duties in any "other state organ, company, or organisation performed by professional members of the army assigned there by an order of an authorised officer (hereinafter assignments outside the army)." Am I correct in my interpretation that those assigned outside the army in this way fall within the category of those who are performing service in the army under Article 8?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Esteemed Mr. Prosecutor, your question was couched in the following terms: Am I correct if my interpretation. You merely read the text contained in Article 8, but I'm yet to hear an interpretation. Which article are you interpreting and in what sense?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me be more direct, General. Under Article 8, somebody assigned outside the army nevertheless is to be considered as performing service in the army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm yet to hear your question. I didn't get a question, I'm sorry. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Apology accepted, sir. Do you agree that officers assigned outside the army are considered under Article 8 to be performing service in the army of the VJ, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Why does Article 8 not say that, sir?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand and as far as the interpretation that I got --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Pause, pause.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Pause. I'm asking you to confine your answer to what is written in Article 8. Under Article 8, service in the army includes military and other duties performed by professional officers signed outside the army, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we have Exhibit P2413 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But not as an officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sorry, General, just before we move on, what do you mean by "but not as an officer"?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Esteemed Mr. Prosecutor, the interpretation I got was you saying is that an officer of the army in a different army, or perhaps I misheard. I may have -- well, perhaps a little, so when what we said comes out, when he is sent to another unit, to the VRS, he is a member of the VRS, a member of that force, yet he performs his function, his duty as an officer. That is what the status of an officer means. You get the status of an officer as soon as you are promoted to the rank of second lieutenant, so the meaning is that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, nowhere in my question did I mention the VRS. We will do this for as long as it takes, sir. My question is this, please answer it this time. Service in the army also includes military and other duties performed by professional members of the army assigned outside the army? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we move, please, to Exhibit P24 -- sorry, my learned friend is on his feet, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm objecting because when Mr. Thomas phrased this previous question and quoted Article 8, paragraph 2, he did not finish reading what it says. He has repeated several times outside the army, yet he never quoted the entire article which says in the federal Defence ministry and other federal organs and then a list of what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm entitled to put to the witness whichever propositions I consider are necessary. If my learned friend wishes to add anything else, he is perfectly entitled to in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we have, exhibit, please, 2413. And let me just check, Your Honours, that can be done in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, this is an order issued by General Perisic on the 9th of November --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May we please zoom in --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I can't see it properly. I see it. I don't see the signature though.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we scroll down, please, Mr. Registrar. Can we please also have the English on the screen for Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, what we see is an order from General Perisic dated the 9th of November, 1995, following the fall of the Krajina and Operation Storm, which occurred in August 1995. You will see that the order is issued with the aim of establishing responsibility and solving status and service for professional soldiers of the Yugoslav Army who served in the 40th Personnel Centre. Now, in this context, General, are we talking about the soldiers who went and fought in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. You will see that the order is for assistant chiefs of the General Staff to study official assessments, statements, and other material regarding all officers of the 40th Personnel Centre that fall within their responsibility, and it sets out a number of proposals dealing with those individuals. My question again, sir, is that in this context we are talking about the officers who went and fought in the SVK, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How many times do you want to ask that question before you are satisfied, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, sir, it's mentioned twice in the document. I just wanted to make sure that we are reading it the right way both times.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, you asked if this was in relation to the members of the 40th Personnel Centre or persons who were handled by the 40th Personnel Centre and were in the SVK, so the answer to your question would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point if I could just have a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You will see, General, a number of measures that are set out in this document, but do you agree that these are effectively the commencement of disciplinary measures against certain individuals?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer the question, may I ask an additional one myself?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just pause, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, you cannot. My question is a straightforward one, sir. Are the measures set out in this order effectively the precursor to or commencement of disciplinary action being taken against certain individuals? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but, if you don't mind, I would like to provide an additional answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Please do, sir.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at the date here, specifically the date this document was produced.
